sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Royal Oak, Michigan?
sections.html:
Royal Oak sellers work with the city's Assessing and Building divisions and with the Oakland County Register of Deeds, and one local variable is whether the house is a registered rental. A house lived in by its owner needs the deed, the transfer affidavits and the tax steps. A rental adds the city's registration and inspection rules.

Royal Oak is an inner-ring suburb about 10 miles north of downtown Detroit, in Oakland County, along the Woodward Corridor and served by I-75 and I-696. It was named in 1819 after a large oak tree that a survey party noticed, became a village in 1891 and was reincorporated as a city in 1921. The city calls itself the city of trees, and the National Arbor Day Foundation has named it a Tree City USA every year since 1976.

Read on for what the Census numbers say about local housing, what a seller owes the city, and the county's rules for getting a deed onto the record.

sections.h2: Why is Royal Oak a strong location for buyers?
sections.html:
Royal Oak has one of the largest downtowns of any Detroit suburb, and buyers pay attention to how close a house sits to it. Since the late 1990s and early 2000s the downtown along Main Street and Washington Avenue has become an entertainment and dining district, and condominium and loft buildings have added residents there.

  • The Detroit Zoo is largely inside the city, with part of it reaching into Huntington Woods.
  • Corewell Health William Beaumont University Hospital is among the city's listed points of interest.
  • The Royal Oak Music Theatre, the Baldwin Theatre and a comedy club draw evening traffic.
  • Arts, Beats and Eats takes over downtown each Labor Day weekend, and the city sponsors events tied to the Woodward Dream Cruise.
  • The Royal Oak Farmers Market has operated since 1925 and sits at 11 Mile Road and Troy Street.

Noise, parking and event traffic are normal questions from buyers touring houses near downtown, so mention event weekends when you describe the street.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show for Royal Oak housing?
sections.html:
Royal Oak's per capita income is $66,293 and its median household income is $101,109. The Census Bureau lists a median value of $328,700 for owner-occupied homes, an owner-occupied rate of 68.0 percent and median gross rent of $1,381 for 2020 to 2024.

The household mix differs from most suburbs. The average household has 1.98 people, 42.3 percent of 2020 households were one person, and only 14.8 percent of residents are under 18. Also, 82.8 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and 64.1 percent of adults 25 and older hold at least a bachelor's degree.

The July 2025 population estimate is 57,583, which is 1.1 percent below the 2020 base. The city peaked at 86,238 in 1970 and has stayed near 57,000 to 58,000 since 2010. With 11.79 square miles of land and about 4,937 people per square mile, a listing here competes with many similar houses in the same school and block pattern, so condition and presentation count for a lot.

sections.h2: Which schools serve Royal Oak houses?
sections.html:
Royal Oak Schools serve the city, and a portion of its land is zoned to Berkley Public Schools, so confirm the district for your address before listing. The public high schools, Dondero and Kimball, were combined into Royal Oak High School in 2006, and the two middle schools were combined into a single Royal Oak Middle School in 2007.

Private options include schools tied to the Shrine of the Little Flower parish. A branch of Oakland Community College is in the city. If you are selling to a household with children, the district boundary is the first question they will ask.

sections.h2: What does Royal Oak require if the house is a rental?
sections.html:
A rental house in Royal Oak must be registered with the city before it is rented, and the Building Division inspects all residential rental units under the Property Maintenance Code. The city's guide asks owners to name a responsible party within 30 miles, post the property address inside the unit, follow occupancy limits and keep working smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers.

Short-term rentals must also carry insurance and give guests the city's Good Neighbor Policy. A registered rental's paperwork is part of what a buyer will want to see, and an unregistered one is a problem to fix before closing. Penalties under the rental ordinance escalate:

Royal Oak rental ordinance penalties
ViolationPenalty
FirstCivil fine of at least $200 plus costs
SecondCivil fine of at least $350 plus costs
ThirdMisdemeanor, fine up to $500, up to 90 days in jail, or both, and registration may be revoked

The Building Division can answer questions at building@romi.gov, and registration fees fund the inspections.

sections.h2: How do Royal Oak taxes and assessments work for a seller?
sections.html:
Royal Oak bills summer taxes due July 31 and winter taxes due February 14, and the city does not accept postmarks as proof of payment. Interest of one-half of 1 percent a month begins August 1 on a late summer bill, and taxes unpaid on March 1 are payable to the Oakland County Treasurer. Summer taxes can be paid in two halves, the first by July 31 and the second by October 31.

The assessor sets assessed value at 50 percent of true cash value, and taxable value is capped by an inflation multiplier until the property transfers. The Assessor's Office analyzes deeds and affidavits on every transferred property, which triggers the uncapping. The city gives buyers a rough method for estimating the new bill: use half the purchase price as taxable value, divide by 1,000 and multiply by the millage rate.

A homeowner who occupied the property before May 1 of the prior year qualifies for the Principal Residence Exemption, which the city says means a rate roughly 15 mills lower than non-homestead property. Appeals start at the March Board of Review, and the July and December sessions correct clerical errors and mutual mistakes. Homeowners can view parcel records free on BS&A Online, which helps you check your property record before a buyer does.

sections.h2: What does Oakland County require before it records a Royal Oak deed?
sections.html:
The Oakland County Register of Deeds checks the paper before it records, so a defective document can cost weeks. The first page needs a 2.5 inch top margin and half-inch margins elsewhere, and the deed must be notarized. Deeds signed before April 6, 2017 had to state the marital status of male grantors, and those signed before March 4, 2002 needed two witnesses.

  • The legal description must clear the county's Sidwell Validation Unit before payment.
  • The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.
  • Copies cost $1.00 a page, plus $5.00 for a certification.

Transfer tax applies to any instrument with consideration above $99.99, and under MCL 207.523 the seller owes it. The county's printed rates are $1.10 per $1,000 for the county and $7.50 per $1,000 for the state.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a rental before selling it in Royal Oak?
faqs.a: The city requires registration before a house is rented, so a rental that is occupied should already be registered. Give the buyer the registration paperwork and ask the Building Division what the new owner must file.

faqs.q: When are Royal Oak property taxes due?
faqs.a: Summer taxes are due July 31 and winter taxes February 14. A summer bill can be paid in halves, with the second half due October 31.

faqs.q: How does the Principal Residence Exemption work after a sale?
faqs.a: The buyer applies for it on the new home, and the city says it lowers the rate by about 15 mills compared with a non-homestead property. Your own exemption should end when you rescind it.

faqs.q: What does Oakland County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: $30.00 per deed, including the $4.00 state survey fee. A warranty deed also needs a $5.00 tax certificate from the county treasurer.

faqs.q: What happens to my taxable value when I sell my Royal Oak house?
faqs.a: It uncaps for the new owner. The Assessor's Office analyzes the deed and affidavit, and the buyer's first bill may reflect a higher taxable value than yours.
